title: Rosalind and the Salt Again
premise: Rafael Okafor, a scribe bound by debt to the Ledger Guild of Vess, discovers the guild has been quietly trading in answered prayers—bottled miracles harvested from gods everyone believed dead. When the old gods wake and begin reclaiming what was taken, the ledgers themselves become doors, and Rafael's careful bookkeeping is the only map through a country being unmade into something older. Hunted by her guildmaster, courted by a resurrected god who remembers her grandmother's name, she must choose between erasing her debts and erasing herself. In the end, Rafael burns the master ledger, dissolving Vess's borders and its debts alike, and walks out through the last remaining door carrying nothing but a pen and one honest page.
about_author: Silas Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing colonial-era trade records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, power, and the people history tries to leave out of its ledgers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Rafael Okafor, POV. A temple scribe deep in debt-bond to the Ledger Guild of Vess, Rafael balances impossible accounts: prayers logged as assets, miracles as inventory. When an entry for a dead god's favor refuses to stay closed, her supervisor warns her to leave it blank. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the first crack in a world built on tidy numbers.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered Collect
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. The closed entry reopens itself overnight, and a petitioner arrives claiming his prayer was answered after forty years. The Guild pays him off and confiscates the miracle—a jarred warmth that hums. Rafael copies the transaction and feels the ink move under her hand. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into complicity; she realizes she has been the machinery of theft.

chapters.title: What the Guild Keeps in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV, with a brief interlude from the god Ashen-Vey. Sent to inventory the vaults, Rafael finds hundreds of bottled answers and, at the bottom, a door that opens onto a country that no longer exists—Vess before the border treaties, whole and sunlit. Ashen-Vey speaks through the jars. Emotional beat: vertigo and temptation; the past is offering her a way out.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Name in an Old Hand
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Digging into provenance records, Rafael learns the Guild's founding miracle was harvested from her own grandmother, a priestess erased from every register but one. Her debt-bond traces back to that theft; she has been paying interest on her family's stolen divinity. Emotional beat: grief igniting into purpose—this is no longer survival, it's inheritance claimed.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Serel, POV. Serel reveals he has always known what Rafael is, and offers full debt-forgiveness if she helps bottle the waking gods before they fully return. He is gentle, reasonable, even loving—and utterly corrupt. Emotional beat: seduction of comfort; Rafael sees how easily justice becomes just another account to balance.

chapters.title: Borders That Forget Themselves
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Refusing Serel, she flees into the old country through the cellar door, but each crossing erases more of present-day Vess—roads reverting to salt marsh, neighbors forgetting their own names. The gods' return isn't salvation; it's a tide. Emotional beat: horror at unintended consequences; her escape is drowning the world she came from.

chapters.title: Ashen-Vey Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael and Ashen-Vey, alternating POV. The risen god offers to restore her grandmother's line and open a permanent door out—if Rafael will write him back into the world as its sole keeper. She recognizes the same bargain Serel made, dressed in holier cloth. Emotional beat: clarity; power always asks to be the only name on the page.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Returning to Vess, Rafael does the one thing a scribe can do against power: a public audit. She reads the true ledgers aloud in the temple square—every stolen prayer, every forged debt, Serel's signature on her grandmother's ruin. The crowd's remembered grievances begin answering back. Emotional beat: defiant courage; words as the last lawful weapon when law itself is bought.

chapters.title: Burning the Master Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV, climax. Serel moves to seal the doors and bottle the crowd's rising prayers; Rafael fights her way to the master ledger and sets it alight with the same miraculous ink she once copied. Debts dissolve, borders unravel, and Ashen-Vey, half-written into the world, chooses at the last moment to help rather than rule—because she wrote him an honest page. Emotional beat: sacrificial triumph at terrible cost.

chapters.title: One Honest Page
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV, resolution. Vess exists now as a country of memory and choice, its people freed of both taxes and temples. Rafael, debtless and nearly anonymous, keeps a small school where children learn to write their own names first. On the final page of a plain new notebook, she writes her grandmother's name, then her own. Emotional beat: earned peace—inheritance fulfilled not as power kept, but as power given away.
